# P-006 — Duplicate index from migration-DDL name vs ORM auto-generated name

- PATTERN_ID: P-006
- ROOT_CAUSE_PATTERN:
  Migration 004 hardcodes `CREATE INDEX ix_feedback_samples_timestamp` (db/migrations.py:79)
  while the ORM column has `index=True` (db/models.py:334), auto-generating
  `ix_feedback_training_samples_timestamp`. The normal provisioning path runs
  create_all AND migrations, so both indexes exist on the same column — duplicate
  write/storage cost with no query benefit.
- ORIGIN_FINDING: FKT-F-006
- SEARCH_METHOD:
  - grep `CREATE INDEX|index=True` (23 hits); diffed each of the 8 migration-004
    index names against SQLAlchemy auto-names (`ix_<table>_<column>`).
  - Live read-only probe: both indexes confirmed present on
    feedback_training_samples(timestamp) in tracker_app/data/sessions.db.
- CANDIDATES: none.
- CONFIRMED_SIBLINGS:
  - None new — the other 7 migration-004 index names match the ORM auto-names
    exactly (models.py:136,142,159,177,230,239,260).
- REJECTED_SIBLINGS:
  - ORM `index=True` columns with no migration DDL (ix_review_history_item_id,
    ix_intent_predictions_timestamp, ix_tracking_sessions_start_time,
    ix_concept_encounters_concept, ix_memory_decay_keyword,
    ix_memory_decay_last_seen_ts, ix_sessions_start_ts): created by create_all in
    every provisioning path (migrations also invoke create_all via
    ensure_base_schema); present in live DB; no divergence.
- OPEN_QUESTIONS:
  - Whether any deployment skips migrations entirely (create_all-only DBs would
    lack ix_feedback_samples_timestamp and thus not exhibit the duplicate) —
    ops-dependent, not observable in-repo.
